keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1918, but 'the declaration was officially approved by the Finnish Parliament on 6 December' 1917 (infobox 6 December 1917) and the RSFSR recognised Finland on 4 January 1918. Same outline as the 1918 shape without Petsamo.

minus.text: Petsamo (Pechenga), the Arctic district with the ice-free port

correction.text: the 1918 outline without Petsamo, which Finland receives by the Treaty of Tartu (14 October 1920)

keyframe_review.note: 376,512 km2 for 1918-1919 against the infobox's 338,455 km2 (no year; ratio 1.11). The outline already holds Petsamo (the gazetteer finds it in all shapes 1918-1944), but the Treaty of Tartu page says 'Finland additionally received Petsamo' in the treaty of 14 October 1920 (the extract adds that Finland 'had already annexed the district from Russia several years earlier', which I cannot reconcile); I follow the treaty as the date of formal acquisition. Aland (4 of 5 probe cells) is inside; no page opened discusses it. The pages opened are silent on the Viena and Aunus expeditions (East Karelia) and on the Aland dispute of 1921.

376,667 km2 for 1920-1939 (ratio 1.11 to the infobox, which is the post-1944 area): the Tartu border with Petsamo. Petsamo is formally Finland's from the treaty of 14 October 1920 (ratified 31 December 1920). The Winter War page says Finland ceded '9% of its territory' in 1940; the 1940 shape is 8.1% smaller.

346,050 km2 for 1940-1941: the Moscow Peace Treaty border ('Finland ceded 9% of its territory': Gulf of Finland islands, Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia, Salla, Rybachy Peninsula). The shape keeps Hanko, leased to the USSR in 1940; the shape starts in January but the treaty is of March 1940 (the 1920 outline holds until then).

correction.text: the Finnish state inside the 1920 outline, with the regained Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia; East Karelia is occupied Soviet land

keyframe_review.note: 447,676 km2 for 1942-1943: includes the military-administered East Karelia, which was Soviet land and not Finnish territory ('On 19 July 1941, the Finns created a military administration in occupied East Karelia'; the advance reached Petrozavodsk, Lake Onega and the Svir by 6 December 1941). Finland's own state is the 1942 outline inside the 1920 outline (it had 'regained its post-Winter War concessions' by September 1941); East Karelia is carried by the occupation events.

correction.text: shape unchanged but valid only from June to September 1944; January-May 1944 is the 1942 state, October-December the 1945 outline

keyframe_review.note: 355,697 km2 for 1944: a mid-1944 snapshot after Vyborg fell on 20 June and Petrozavodsk by 28 June 1944 (gazetteer: Vyborg mostly out, Sortavala still in, East Karelia out, Petsamo in). January to May 1944 holds the 1942 state; after the armistice of 19 September 1944 the border is that of 1940 without Petsamo (the 1945 shape). The shape is valid only for June to September 1944.

337,169 km2 for 1945-2023, ratio 1.00 to the infobox's 338,455 km2 (0.996): the 1940 border without Petsamo ('The new armistice also handed all of Petsamo to the Soviet Union'). The shape keeps Porkkala, leased to the USSR in September 1944 for 50 years and returned in 1956 (occupation pair in the ledger).
337,169 km2, unchanged since 1945; ratio 1.00 to the infobox.

region.text: the Grand Duchy of Finland as the independent state of December 1917, without Petsamo (received 1920)

ledger.note: 1917, 6 December: Finland declares independence. 'The declaration was officially approved by the Finnish Parliament on 6 December' (infobox 6 December 1917); 'the RSFSR was the first country to recognise Finland's independence on 4 January 1918'. The page gives the grand duchy's land as 'Finland', not a boundary.

1919, 17 July: the republican constitution. 'Constitution established: 17 July 1919'; 'a republican constitution was adopted and Finland became a presidential republic', with Stahlberg elected president on 25 July 1919. Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Petsamo (Pechenga), the Arctic district with the ice-free port

ledger.note: 1920, 14 October: the Treaty of Tartu gives Finland Petsamo. 'Finland additionally received Petsamo, with its ice-free harbour on the Arctic Ocean'; signed 14 October 1920, ratifications exchanged on 31 December 1920. Finland gave up Repola and Porajarvi in East Karelia, which it had occupied in the Viena and Aunus expeditions (not dated by the page), and handed North Ingria to Russia.

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1939, 30 November: the Soviet Union invades. The Winter War begins with 'a Soviet invasion of Finland on 30 November 1939'; the Red Army's first conquest is Terijoki on the Karelian Isthmus. The zone is the land later ceded (the page lists Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia, Salla, Rybachy Peninsula).

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1940, 13 March: the Winter War ends with the Moscow Peace Treaty (the Finland page: signed 12 March, 'the war ended the following day'; the Winter War page: 13 March 1940).

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1940, March: Finland cedes the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia. 'Finland ceded 9% of its territory to the Soviet Union' including 'Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia'; the Finland page: 'Soviet forces reached Vyborg' and Finland lost 'its second-largest city, Vyborg'.

region.text: Salla, the Rybachy Peninsula and the Gulf of Finland islands

ledger.note: 1940, March: Finland also cedes Salla, the Rybachy Peninsula and islands in the Gulf of Finland to the Soviet Union (the page's list: 'Cession of the Gulf of Finland islands, Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia, Salla, Rybachy Peninsula').

region.text: the Hanko Peninsula, leased to the Soviet Union

ledger.note: 1940, March: Hanko is leased to the Soviet Union. The treaty result includes a 'lease of Hanko to the Soviet Union'; the page gives the 30-year length only for the October 1939 proposal.

1941: Hanko is back in Finnish hands. The Continuation War infobox lists 'Hanko retaken by Finland' as a territorial change; the page extract gives no date, so the year is the researcher's bridging (page silent).

region.text: East Karelia: the land the 1942 shape holds beyond the 1920 outline (Petrozavodsk, Lake Onega, the Svir)

ledger.note: 1941, 19 July: Finland occupies East Karelia. 'On 19 July 1941, the Finns created a military administration in occupied East Karelia'; the Army of Karelia attacked towards Petrozavodsk, Lake Onega and the Svir on 9 September, and its advance had halted by 6 December 1941.

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1941, September: Finland regains the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia. 'Finnish forces captured Vyborg on 29 August'; 'By September 1941, Finland had regained its post-Winter War concessions to the Soviet Union in Karelia.'

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1944, June: the Soviet offensive reaches the Karelian Isthmus. 'The Soviet Vyborg-Petrozavodsk offensive in June and August 1944 drove the Finns from most of the territories that they had gained'; the Red Army 'recaptured Viipuri with insignificant resistance on 20 June'.

region.text: East Karelia: the land the 1942 shape holds beyond the 1920 outline (Petrozavodsk, Lake Onega, the Svir)

ledger.note: 1944, June: Finland loses East Karelia. Petrozavodsk was recaptured 'by 28 June 1944'; the offensive ran June to August. The year and the main town are the page's, the end of the occupation of all of East Karelia within the month is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1944, 19 September: the Moscow Armistice ends the Continuation War between Finland and the Soviet Union (and the United Kingdom).

region.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1944, 19 September: the armistice restores the 1940 border. 'The Armistice restored the Moscow Peace Treaty of 1940, with a number of modifications'; Finland loses the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia regained in 1941.

region.text: Petsamo (Pechenga), the Arctic district with the ice-free port

ledger.note: 1944, 19 September: Finland cedes Petsamo. 'The new armistice also handed all of Petsamo to the Soviet Union.'

region.text: the Porkkala Peninsula west of Helsinki

ledger.note: 1944, 19 September: Finland leases Porkkala to the Soviet Union. 'Finland was further compelled to lease Porkkala to the Soviet Union for a period of fifty years.'
1956: the Soviet Union returns Porkkala. 'Porkkala was returned to Finland in 1956.' The page gives no month.

wars.name: Finnish Civil War
wars.outcome: On 27 January 1918 'the government began to disarm the Russian forces' in Ostrobothnia, which led to 'a short but bitter civil war'. The Finland page extract gives no end date and does not name the Reds' state or the front.
wars.note: Zones left empty because no page opened names them; the rebel state needs a dossier (finnish-socialist-workers-republic, type rebel).

wars.name: Winter War

zones.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia

wars.outcome: Soviet invasion of 30 November 1939; Moscow Peace Treaty of 13 March 1940 (12 March signed per the Finland page): Finland cedes 9% of its territory and leases Hanko.
wars.note: The Soviet puppet 'Finnish Democratic Republic' (Terijoki government) was formed on 1 December 1939 and held no land beyond Terijoki.

wars.name: Continuation War

zones.text: the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg and Ladoga Karelia
East Karelia: the land the 1942 shape holds beyond the 1920 outline (Petrozavodsk, Lake Onega, the Svir)

wars.outcome: Finnish declaration of war 25 June 1941; Vyborg taken 29 August 1941; East Karelia occupied from 19 July 1941; Soviet offensive from June 1944 (Viipuri 20 June, Petrozavodsk by 28 June); Moscow Armistice of 19 September 1944: 1940 border restored, Petsamo ceded, Porkkala leased for 50 years.
wars.note: The page gives no area for the peak of the occupation.

wars.name: Lapland War
wars.outcome: The armistice required Finland to drive German troops out, 'the Lapland War of 1944-1945, when Finland fought retreating German forces in northern Finland'; no border moved.

certainty.note: Petsamo, East Karelia and the Aland Islands were unsettled until the Treaty of Tartu (1920) and the 1921 Aland decision (not on the pages opened).
Treaty of Tartu border to the Winter War; the Moscow Peace Treaty border from March 1940.
Front lines and the East Karelian military administration moved within the year; the 1940 border is sharp again from 19 September 1944.
The 1940 border without Petsamo; Porkkala leased to the USSR until 1956.

notes: Page budget 5 of 5 used (Finland, Winter War, Continuation War, Treaty of Tartu, Moscow Armistice). Cliopatria 'Republic of Finland' 1918..2024 (7 shapes) is one state; Q33 is not shared. Counterparts needing dossiers: finnish-socialist-workers-republic (Red Finland, 1918, type rebel, the front and end date are not on any page opened); republic-of-north-ingria and the East Karelian formations (Uhtua republic, Viena and Aunus expeditions, 1918-1920) are not on the pages opened. Page silent: the end of the civil war, the Aland dispute and League decision of 1921, the dates of the Viena and Aunus expeditions, the date Hanko returned to Finland (Continuation War infobox 'Hanko retaken by Finland'), the Karelo-Finnish SSR date on the Winter War page, the Paris Peace Treaty day (1947), the area of the occupied East Karelia. Disagreement: the Finland page says the Moscow Peace Treaty was signed on 12 March 1940, the Winter War page gives 13 March; the Tartu page extract says Finland 'had already annexed' Petsamo earlier, which is not reconciled with 'additionally received' in 1920. Gazetteer names needed: Petsamo, Karelian Isthmus, Ladoga Karelia, Salla, Rybachy Peninsula, Hanko (place), East Karelia. Cliopatria's 1918 shape holds Petsamo (and probably Aland); verdict adjust. The extract tool returns model-written summaries: quoted phrases are the extracts' renderings.
